extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of German literature, literary historians, and creative writers studying poetic and philosophical style
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards for judging the quality, style, and cultural value of German philosophy, prose, and poetry (especially from the 16th–18th centuries), including language, originality, moral force, and popular resonance. Useful for literary-historical evaluation and creative-writing judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Erudition and knowledge of antiquity
rubrics_metrics.description: The German writers' erudition — being 'full of recollections and ideas of that philosophy of antiquity' — preserved them from extreme error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valued: deep learning and explicit recollection of classical/antique sources. Effect: anchors thought, prevents reckless novelty. Anti-pattern: lack of classical learning leading to shallow or extravagant modern errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance between scholarly revival and original progress
rubrics_metrics.description: Leibnitz is criticised for being 'too fond of reviving exploded difficulties' even while acting as a harbinger of deeper inquiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good work may revive old problems usefully, but excessive revival of exhausted difficulties is a fault. Aim for scholarship that stimulates genuine new investigation rather than merely re-running past controversies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral nobility and purity of ethical thought
rubrics_metrics.description: Spinosa's morality, though not Christian, is described as 'a pure and noble morality resembling that of the ancient Stoics'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess moral systems for nobility and purity of ethical sentiment regardless of doctrinal alignment. A morality can be valuable even if its metaphysics are judged erroneous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination of intellectual clarity and heartfelt conviction
rubrics_metrics.description: Spinosa's strength is not merely 'scientific clearness and decision of his intellect' but 'the open-heartedness, strong feeling and conviction' that seem to gush from his heart and soul.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work that pairs rigorous reasoning with evident passion and conviction is more persuasive and enduring. Anti-pattern: cold technical clarity without emotional or moral force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and independence of thought
rubrics_metrics.description: Leibnitz's philosophy is criticised for being 'entirely devoted to the spirit and necessities of his time' and not coming 'forward in the independence and confidence of its own original power.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value ideas that assert independent, original perspectives rather than primarily serving as polemics against contemporaries. Polemic-only work is less admirable than genuinely novel systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophical dignity respecting human nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Leibnitz's watchmaker metaphor and related hypotheses 'tend to give a degrading view of the nobler part of our nature.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer philosophies that maintain the dignity and nobility of human nature; avoid reductions that portray humanity in purely mechanical or degrading terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solutions satisfactory to feeling and conscience
rubrics_metrics.description: Theodicy and other clever solutions (Leibnitzian optimism or Spartan alternatives) are rejected as unsatisfactory 'either to feeling or to philosophy.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Philosophical explanations should cohere with moral feeling and the voice of conscience, not merely display intellectual dexterity. Anti-pattern: elegant but emotionally or morally unconvincing rationalizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conception of time and space that ennobles
rubrics_metrics.description: Antiquity saw time and place as 'an endless theatre for the display of the eternal' producing 'stupendous feeling'; Leibnitz reduced them to 'the arrangement of contemporary or consecutive incidents.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In poetic and philosophical treatment, prefer conceptions of time/space that elevate and enlarge the soul rather than deaden it into mere succession of events. Anti-pattern: treating time/space as purely mechanical or insignificant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of scholastic formalism
rubrics_metrics.description: A sect 'confined to schools' becomes 'a mere being of formality' where ideas are 'no longer ideas' but 'mere formulas.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value living, vital thought over rigid adherence to received formulas. Beware of systems that ossify into empty jargon divorced from genuine insight or feeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution to national language and cultural resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Leibnitz and Wolf are credited with giving 'a new spring to the study of the German language, history, and antiquities' and thereby serving the language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess writers by the extent to which they enrich and develop the national tongue, idiom, and cultural heritage. Contributions that deepen linguistic resources are praiseworthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power, life, and simplicity of expression (Luther model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Luther's Bible-translation is 'the standard and model of classical expression' in High Dutch and is said to impart 'power, life, and simplicity' to German writers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor prose and poetry marked by energetic clarity, accessible phrasing, and simple dignity. Example: Biblical cadences entering into common language. Anti-pattern: overstylized, artificial diction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revolutionary/popular eloquence and passion
rubrics_metrics.description: Luther displays 'revolutionary eloquence' and his writings reveal 'marks of mighty internal conflict' — 'a struggle between light and darkness, faith and passion.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writing aimed at the people that channels fervent conviction and moral struggle is powerful. Prize passionate, direct address and rhetorical force when speaking to popular audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility and respect for popular intellect
rubrics_metrics.description: The common people of Germany 'has displayed so much profoundness of intellect' and the author asserts 'the voice of the people is the voice of God.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good writing should respect and address the intelligence of ordinary readers; clarity and depth that reach popular audiences is a virtue. Anti-pattern: elitist obscurity that underestimates common readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity of popular poetry: heroic fragments and vernacular voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Popular poetry consists partly of 'songs, solitary fragments of a departed age of heroism' and partly of 'the productions of the vulgar themselves.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value works that preserve authentic folk-material, heroic memory, and vernacular expression. Authenticity and rootedness in popular forms are key merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventiveness, richness, and poetical power (Meistersanger model)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Meistersanger is praised as 'an artificer in poetry... full of power and fancy... more inventive than Chaucer, more rich... more poetical.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess poets for originality of imagination, richness of material, and strong poetic invention. High inventiveness and abundant fancy are positive qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetical fancy, depth of feeling, and natural vigour (Jacob Bohme)
rubrics_metrics.description: Jacob Bohme has 'ardent imagination', 'poetical fancy', 'fulness of fancy and depth of feeling', and his language shows 'strength and richness' and 'a charm of nature, simplicity, and unsought vigour.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prize imaginative intensity, genuine feeling, and natural, unforced vigor in language. Anti-pattern: learned but lifeless phrasing that lacks natural charm.

rubrics_metrics.name: National sentiment and power to found a new epoch (Klopstock)
rubrics_metrics.description: Klopstock 'stood conspicuous... in respect of his intensely national feelings' and with the Messiad 'the new literature of our country may be said to begin.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works that translate national feeling into poetry and can inaugurate a new literary epoch are of greatest value. Criterion: national resonance and transformative cultural influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mastery of elegiac feeling: gradation, blending, depth
rubrics_metrics.description: Klopstock's most successful poetry 'is that conceived in the spirit of elegy. Every gradation, blending, and depth of elegiac feeling is handled by him with the power and ease of a master.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate elegiac poetry by the subtlety of its gradations, the smoothness of blending emotional tones, and depth of melancholy. Mastery = effortless control over these elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal, experiential, and descriptive vividness (Flemming)
rubrics_metrics.description: Flemming's poetry is 'intensely personal... filled with the inspiration of his own friendships, passions, and loves' and his travel-descriptions are 'with the most glowing feeling, and a truly oriental splendour of fancy.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prize poetry and prose that draws on lived experience and renders scenes with vivid, glowing description. Emotional intimacy and colourful depiction strengthen work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of affectation, artifice, and slavish imitation
rubrics_metrics.description: The post-war period degenerated into 'a mere artificial and fantastic display of insignificant thoughts upon worthless subjects' and writers were 'addicted to imitation' of French/English poets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Negative criteria: avoid affectation, artificiality, and moral or stylistic triviality; avoid slavish imitation of foreign fashions that suppress native feeling. Seek authenticity over fashionable mimicry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivation of language despite stylistic carelessness
rubrics_metrics.description: Even poets 'careless, frequently corrupt' in language (Haller, Gleim) must be regarded as great relative to the barbarism they escaped.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging historical writers, allow for contextual advances: a poet may have linguistic faults yet still be meritorious for raising literature above worse conditions. Balance critique with historical perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of patronage and fostering young talent
rubrics_metrics.description: A monarch should 'foster and cherish talents not yet completely developed, and furnish young men with the instruments and opportunities of distinction.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultural institutions and patrons are judged by how well they nurture emerging writers; positive support should encourage diversity and freedom rather than narrow academies that produce tame work.
